clue.text: Dissolute character given stick on Cornish river

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip
a staff is a walking stick or rod

explanation.surface: A dissolute rambler is handed a walking stick beside a Cornish river.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means placed after, so the stick follows the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, drunken, debauched knight, a byword for dissolute living.

clue.text: Opposite view of expert

blocks.note: a facet is an aspect or view of something
taken as written
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert's view is the contrary one.
explanation.walkthrough: The word breaks differently from the answer's spaces: FACET OF ACE regroups as FACE TO FACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting face to face means sitting opposite someone, looking directly at each other.

clue.text: Drag fish over to the sheltered side

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

blocks.note: to draw is to drag or pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler hauls a fish across to calmer water.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward means on or towards the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: Robber, one caught by the force's leader

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
caught by means held by, so the single letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
the first letter of force

explanation.surface: A robber is arrested by the chief of police.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside THE, and F follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is someone who steals, and a robber is a thief who uses force.

clue.text: Varnish in two languages

blocks.note: French and Polish are two European languages

explanation.surface: A word for varnish is given in two different tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests translation; instead the two language names themselves join to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a shellac varnish rubbed on to give furniture a high gloss.

clue.text: Immediate help for the forgetful actor

blocks.note: first meaning: done without delay
second meaning: a line whispered from the wings to an actor who has dried

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like urgent assistance in a theatre; the adjective and the noun are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something done at once and a noun for a cue given to an actor who forgets lines.

clue.text: Considerable mistake making journey there and back

blocks.note: a round sum is a considerable one
a trip is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A big error leads to a return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey to a place and back again, an outward and return leg.

clue.text: Crazy about North American star

blocks.note: mad means crazy
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: A fan is wild about an American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy about' reads as one phrase meaning besotted with; the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is the American pop singer, one of the biggest music stars of all time.

clue.text: Call for a spell

blocks.note: first meaning: to name or designate
second meaning: a period of time

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests summoning magic; 'spell' is a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to name something; as a noun it is a fixed period of time.

clue.text: Form of comic verse delivered by clergyman snubbed by ambassador and wife

indicators.note: to snub is literally to cut short, so the word loses its tail

blocks.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Some light verse is recited by a vicar who has been cold-shouldered by a diplomat and his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: His Excellency is the formal title of an ambassador; 'snubbed' is used in its literal sense of cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a four-line humorous biographical poem, named after its inventor Edmund Clerihew Bentley.

clue.text: Kill famous steeplechaser in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Red Rum won the Grand National, Britain's great steeplechase, three times in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Someone plans to do away with a champion racehorse now put out to grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum's name famously spells a sinister word backwards, as used in The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: To murder is to kill unlawfully and deliberately; both are verbs for ending a life.

clue.text: One may be fed by the roadside

definitions.text: One may be fed by the roadside

blocks.clueFragment: One may be fed by the roadside
blocks.note: surface reading: an animal or traveller given food at the edge of a road
setter's reading: coins are fed into a kerbside machine to pay for leaving a car

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' suggests food; here coins are fed into a slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers put coins into this kerbside device to pay for time parked in the space beside it.

clue.text: A poor piece of parking? Fine by me!

definitions.text: A poor piece of parking? Fine by me!

blocks.clueFragment: A poor piece of parking? Fine by me!
blocks.note: surface reading: a relaxed driver shrugging off bad parking as perfectly acceptable
setter's reading: the speaker is the official who will issue a fine for that bad parking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine by me' normally means 'that's all right with me'; here it means the speaker hands out the penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who patrols streets ticketing badly parked cars is the one who issues fines for poor parking.

clue.text: Sonnet king composed in part of London

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch wrote a sonnet in a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington is a wealthy district in west London, home to the palace and museums.

clue.text: G-man, on horseback, becomes bored

blocks.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, called a Fed in US slang
a jockey riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: A government agent riding a horse grows weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fed up means being bored and tired of something, an idiom for weary dissatisfaction.

clue.text: A variety of men phone foremost of antiquaries for remarkable things

indicators.note: a variety means a mixed assortment, so the letters come out in a different order
foremost means at the very front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of antiquaries

explanation.surface: Assorted men ring the leading antique dealers about some extraordinary finds.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena, plural of phenomenon, are remarkable or exceptional occurrences or people.

clue.text: Impassive expression in card game given by female with ace

blocks.note: poker is a betting card game
F is the standard abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman holding an ace keeps a straight face during a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker face is a deadpan look giving nothing away, as poker players use to hide their hand.

clue.text: Governor can holding girl

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Stella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A ruler is able to keep hold of a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, 'is able to'; it is just the three letters that wrap round the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan is the governor or keeper of a castle.

clue.text: Give an impression of drunken guests drinking gallons

indicators.note: drunken people stagger about in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
drinking means taking something in, so one letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Tipsy guests knocking back gallons of drink hint at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixing comes first; the gallons letter is then dropped into the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something is to hint at it or give an impression of it without stating it.

clue.text: Chooses tools for breaking up rock

blocks.note: first meaning: selects
second meaning: pointed iron tools on long handles used for digging

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone selecting quarrying gear; the verb and the plural noun are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning selects and as a plural noun for pickaxes used on hard ground.

clue.text: Almost pick up the lot, a whistle

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word is cut short by its final letter

blocks.note: to catch is to pick up, as an illness or a ball
the lot means everything, all of it

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gathers everything up, then lets out a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a loud whistle or jeer of disapproval or crude attention.

clue.text: Freight train crashed, crushing a male, a charitable soul

indicators.note: something crashed is wrecked and jumbled, so these letters are thrown into a new order
crushing pulls the following letters into the wreck so they are mixed in with the rest

blocks.note: goods is the British term for freight, as in a goods train
taken as written
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male
taken as written; the second a in the clue

explanation.surface: A freight train derails and runs over a man, and some kind person comes to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freight train' reads as one thing, but freight is GOODS and the train alone is mixed with A, M and A.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable in Luke's gospel, a Good Samaritan is anyone who generously helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Lear's daughter, for example, hurried ouside

indicators.note: outside (misspelt in the source) means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: ran means hurried
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: One of King Lear's daughters, for instance, rushed out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's two treacherous elder daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: I study a devotional painting

blocks.note: taken as written
to con is an old word for to study or learn

explanation.surface: Someone describes examining a religious picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a devotional painting of a holy figure, especially in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Intelligent Conservative at bar

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A bright Tory politician is spotted in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but is a crowbar-like rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and intelligent are synonyms for mentally quick and bright.

clue.text: Showing little activity, deer tracked by new worker

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
N is the abbreviation for new
a worker ant; ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A sluggish deer is followed by a new hand on the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracked by' means followed by, so the deer comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagnant economy or market is sluggish and shows little growth or movement.

clue.text: Boy trapped in station at Hanoi

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so the name sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of station, all of at, and the start of Hanoi

explanation.surface: A lad is stuck at a railway station in Hanoi.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathan is a boy's name; 'boy' is the crossword cue for a male first name.

clue.text: Statesman, outspoken Liberal holding office

blocks.note: frank means candid and outspoken
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a party in power is said to be in

explanation.surface: An outspoken Liberal politician has a government post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' looks like a container signal, but 'holding office' is one phrase meaning in power.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was an American statesman and one of the Founding Fathers.
